Playing tip to transport units by ship from ports to ports (conquest of unoccupied ports is therefore possible but this costs air mission points):
1. Select a unit, click on strategic transport button (on the lower left).
2. Move the unit from any PORT hex to any unoccupied or friendly PORT hex.
3. From the destination PORT hex you can still move normally infantry units, whereas other unit types cannot move anymore during the same turn.

Kherson - August 10th, 1941

With victory at Uman secured, the Leibstandarte moved south to take the city of Cherson.  During the march another attrocity is alleged to have taken place.  According to a postwar account of a Waffen-SS journalist serving with the 4th Battalion, east of Gejgova, men from the battalion found the mutilated bodies of six fellow SS soldiers who had been captured and executed at the town's NKVD headquarters.  In reprisal, Dietrich ordered the Leibstandarte to shoot all surrendering Soviet troops for three days, and in the ensuing slaughter an estimated 4,000 were killed.  The allegations remain unproven.

On the 27th of September, the Soviets launched a counter offensive aimed at the German southern flank.  It was a strong attack which breached the 3rd Romanian Army and Germany's XXX Armeekorps sector of the front and threatened an envelopment.  The Leibstandarte and elite German mountain divisions were rushed into the line to halt the attack, and then to force them back.

First contact with British troops was made north of Vevi at 11:00 on 10 April. An intercepted radio message indicated that the British command was surprised by the swiftness of the Leibstandarte's thrust and gave orders for immediate withdrawal from the Vermion Position. The SS troops seized Vevi on 11 April, but were stopped a short distance south of that town, where strong Australian forces held the dominating heights overlooking the pass road. During the next day the Leibstandarte reconnoitered the enemy positions and at dusk launched a frontal attack against the pass. After heavy fighting the Leibstandarte overcame the enemy resistance and broke through the defile.

This city is crucial to our overall plan, which is to flank Moscow and attack it from the north where the Soviet defenses are the least ready for a large-scale attack. The formidable and determined Soviet forces will give you a tough fight, Commander. The spy's information points to a submarine pen in southern Greece. The Soviets are developing new advanced submarines there that could disrupt Allied shipping and bring our war effort crashing to a halt. Unfortunately, Greece is currently being invaded by the Soviets, and our troops are stretched too wide to help them. Take your troops in, destroy those bloody submarines and get back before the main army discovers your force. The French have pledged their navy to assist us in this operation.

Welcome back, Commander. It's been roughly 2 months since your destruction of the Soviet submarine pen in Sweden, and almost all of Scandanavia is back under Allied control. However, your next assignment is far from the Scandanavian region, in the vicinity of Salerno, Italy. Italy was a hotspot for much of the early war. Eventually the combined might of British and French forces pushed the Soviet forces back into the sea, making it a safe haven for Allied weapon testing. The Soviets have learned of a very important development in our tests going on here at Salerno, however, and have landed a sizeable force to stop our development process.

This cannot happen, Commander. The weapons being tested here are crucial to our survival against increasingly well armed Soviet forces. Your job is to reinforce the badly beaten garrison of our base to the north, then to retake the area from the cowardly bastards.
Good luck Commander. You'll bloody well need it!!!
Welcome back, Commander. I hope you enjoyed your vacation, but things
have erupted out of control. Stalin, apparently getting desperate at the outcome of the war, has begun building nuclear weapons.

A Soviet scientist wishes to defect to our cause, bringing with him intimate knowledge of Stalin's nuclear weapon program. However, there is a limited gap of time for us to rescue him from the Soviet base in Riga before Soviet units arrive to reinforce the base. Our forces have begun an amphibious landing in the area. Secure the area as quickly and efficently as possible, to retrieve the scientist's crucial information and also to begin the liberation of the Baltic states.
